## Goal

<a id="TrustedExtensions"></a>

### Kinds and views that can be trusted

`TrustedExtensions` · `src/laws.ts:20`

A kind or a view takes part in the compilation only once it keeps its laws, whoever wrote it. A new kind needs no change to the engine; a faulty one is refused before it misleads a document.

- Owner: trame
- Served by: [The laws are requirements](engine.md#LawsAreRequirements)
- Refined by: [Answers without crashing](#AnswersWithoutCrashing), [A blocking hole has an owner](#BlockingHoleHasOwner), [The resolution returns only what it is given](#ClosedResolution), [Complete declaration](#CompleteDeclaration), [Complete declaration of a view](#CompleteViewDeclaration), [Produces only the intermediate format](#IntermediateFormatOnly), [Same input, same answer](#SameInputSameAnswer), [Without evidence, the status is unknown](#UnknownWithoutEvidence)

## Requirements

<a id="AnswersWithoutCrashing"></a>

### Answers without crashing

`AnswersWithoutCrashing` · `src/laws.ts:111` · status: **held**

A function of a kind answers on any value it may be given. Reading an undecided value stops it: that is a decision to take, not a crash; any other error is. A view may not stop: a document cannot wait.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (end: CallEnd, mayStop: boolean): boolean => !end.threw || (mayStop && end.undecided)
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)
- Used by: [Laws](engine.md#Laws), [Views](engine.md#Views)

<a id="AnswersWithoutCrashingCriteria"></a>

**Criteria of the answers without crashing · owner: trame**

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| An answer keeps the law | passed |
| A kind stopped by an undecided value keeps it | passed |
| A view stopped by an undecided value breaks it | passed |
| Any other error breaks it | passed |

<a id="BlockingHoleHasOwner"></a>

### A blocking hole has an owner

`BlockingHoleHasOwner` · `src/laws.ts:139` · status: **held**

A hole that blocks names who must fill it: the hole's own owner, or else the owner of its node.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (hole: ReportedHole, nodeOwner?: string): boolean => hole.severity !== Severity.blocking || Boolean(hole.owner ?? nodeOwner)
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)
- Used by: [Laws](engine.md#Laws)

<a id="ClosedResolution"></a>

### The resolution returns only what it is given

`ClosedResolution` · `src/laws.ts:228` · status: **held**

Settling claims orders the claimants, or names an arbiter among them: it returns no node that claims nothing.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript

```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)

<a id="CompleteDeclaration"></a>

### Complete declaration

`CompleteDeclaration` · `src/laws.ts:64` · status: **held**

A kind has a label, names that the API does not reserve, edges towards kinds that exist (or towards any kind), at most one field for its owner; it settles claims only if it makes some, and its claims target nodes.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (d: KindDeclaration, known: KnownNames): DeclarationFaults => ({
    unlabelled: !d.labelled,
    reserved: d.names.filter((n) => known.reserved.has(n)),
    unknownTargets: d.targets.filter(([, t]) => t !== known.any && !known.kinds.has(t)),
    severalOwners: counts.several(d.ownerFields),
    resolveWithoutClaims: d.resolves && !d.claims,
    claimsOffNodes: d.claimsOffNodes,
  })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Parameters: `counts` ← [Counts](../std/releases/0.17.0/docs/algebra.md#Counts)
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)
- Used by: [Laws](engine.md#Laws)

<a id="CompleteDeclarationCriteria"></a>

**Criteria of the complete declaration · owner: trame**

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| A sound declaration has no fault | passed |
| A name the API reserves is a fault | passed |
| An edge towards an unknown kind is a fault; towards any kind, it is not | passed |
| Two owner fields are a fault | passed |
| Settling claims without making any is a fault | passed |

<a id="CompleteViewDeclaration"></a>

### Complete declaration of a view

`CompleteViewDeclaration` · `src/laws.ts:273` · status: **held**

A view has a name of its own and a label; it belongs to the node's views, or says to which nodes it applies, only if it writes one document per node.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (v: ViewDeclaration): ViewDeclarationFaults => ({
    unnamed: !v.named,
    duplicate: v.duplicate,
    nodeGroupNotPerNode: v.nodeGroup && !v.perNode,
    appliesNotPerNode: v.applies && !v.perNode,
  })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)
- Used by: [Views](engine.md#Views)

<a id="CompleteViewDeclarationCriteria"></a>

**Criteria of the declaration of a view · owner: trame**

|---|---|
| A view of the node, per node, has no fault | passed |
| A view of the node that is not per node has two | passed |
| A name taken twice is a fault | passed |

<a id="IntermediateFormatOnly"></a>

### Produces only the intermediate format

`IntermediateFormatOnly` · `src/laws.ts:318` · status: **held**

A view writes a document of the intermediate format: data that survive being written and read back, with no function, in blocks whose types the format knows. The renderers, and the page, need nothing else.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (d: WrittenDocument, known: ReadonlySet<string>): SerialFaults => ({
    notSerial: d.readBack !== d.text || d.text.includes(d.functionMark),
    unknownBlock: d.blockTypes.find((t) => !known.has(t)),
  })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)
- Used by: [Views](engine.md#Views)

<a id="IntermediateFormatOnlyCriteria"></a>

**Criteria of the intermediate format · owner: trame**

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| Plain data in known blocks keep the law | passed |
| A value lost on the way back breaks it | passed |
| A function breaks it | passed |
| A block of an unknown type is named | passed |

<a id="OrderFree"></a>

### The resolution does not depend on the order

`OrderFree` · `src/laws.ts:207` · status: **held**

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

<a id="SameInputSameAnswer"></a>

### Same input, same answer

`SameInputSameAnswer` · `src/laws.ts:184` · status: **held**

Called twice on the same input, a function of a kind gives the same answer; run twice on the same graph, a view gives the same document. The answers are compared as written.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (answers: readonly string[]): boolean => !counts.several(new Set(answers))
```

</details>

<a id="UnknownWithoutEvidence"></a>

### Without evidence, the status is unknown

`UnknownWithoutEvidence` · `src/laws.ts:161` · status: **held**

A kind says that a node holds, or is violated, only from evidence: a measure or an evaluation. Before any, its status is unknown, blocked, or none.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (status: Status | undefined, evidence: boolean): boolean => evidence || (status !== Status.held && status !== Status.violated)
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Kinds and views that can be trusted](#TrustedExtensions)
- Used by: [Laws](engine.md#Laws)
